PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

Welcome to the meeting of the Parks, Recreation & Community Services Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs and videotapes of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling
(818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

minutes_text:
PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION
  MEETING MINUTES
  Monday, May 20, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 2:38 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Kalfayan, Michals, Wolfson, and President Asatryan
  Absent: Commissioner Babaian

  A.  Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the May 20, 2019, regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall
  on or before Friday, May 17, 2019.
2.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  A. Volunteer Recognition
  Patty Betancourt, Community Services Specialist, gave a brief report regarding the number of
  volunteers and volunteer hours provided in the Community Services & Parks Department during
  the March 1, 2018 – February 28, 2019, reporting period. Volunteers were recognized by the
  department and the Commission and were given a certificate.
3.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian read a list of upcoming City Council agenda
  items related to the Community Services & Parks Department (CSP).
4.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  Ms. Moreno Hernandez announced upcoming events organized or sponsored by the Community
  Services & Parks Department.
5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None
6.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on March 18, 2019.
  Ms. Moreno Hernandez informed the Commission of an error in the minutes that Commissioner
  Wolfson had made her aware of: in the first sentence under item 3, the name “Wilson” should be
  changed to “Wolfson.” She recommended that the minutes be approved with that correction.

  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Wolfson

  That the minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on March 18, 2019, be approved
  as corrected.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes:  Commissioners Kalfayan, Michals, and Wolfson
  1
   Noes:  None
  Absent:  Babaian
  Abstain:  Asatryan

7.  ACTION ITEMS
  A. Glendale Heritage Garden Fitness Equipment & Playground Replacement Project
  1.  Motion to note and file a report regarding the Glendale Heritage Garden Fitness
  Equipment & Playground Replacement Project
  Deputy Director Koko Panossian, provided a PowerPoint presentation including the following
  topics: Glendale Heritage Garden location, size, and amenities; staff meeting with community
  members; trellis shade; fitness equipment location; proposed fitness equipment; playground
  equipment; tentative schedule; and estimated project costs.

  Commissioners had questions and comments about the shade structure and plants, controlling
  the hours of operation of the playground’s sound feature, not sacrificing any trees (staff
  confirmed no trees will be removed), donating the existing spider web play feature, use of the
  park by the non-profit organization occupying the house on the premises, swings not being
  included in the playground, and the possibility of adding more trees through the Arbor Day
  program to create additional shade. Commissioners all expressed concern that there will be
  no shade in the trellis area for two years while the plants grow in and suggested that staff look
  into a temporary shade option.

  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Michals

  That the Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Commission hereby notes and
  files the report regarding the Glendale Heritage Garden Fitness Equipment &
  Playground Replacement Project.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Kalfayan, Michals, Wolfson, and President Asatryan
  Noes: None
  Absent: Babaian
  Abstain: None

8.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Annual Volunteer Report
  A written report was submitted. A verbal report was given during item 2A.

  B.  Customer Service Office and Filming Annual Report
  Gabrielle Goglia, Sr. Community Services Supervisor, gave a report and PowerPoint presentation
  covering the following topics: community building reservations, park reservations, film permits, and
  fiscal impact.

  President Asatryan asked if there was more outreach done that resulted in the increase in film
  permits and how Glendale compares to neighboring cities in terms of film permits issued.

  C.  Contract Class Annual Report
  Ms. Goglia provided a report and PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics: contract
  classes offered, contract class registration, and contract class revenue. She also mentioned that a
  new supervisor with marketing experience is now overseeing the program.

  2
   Commissioner Michals asked if staff knows the reason for the downward trend in sports classes.

  D.  Sparr Heights Community Center Annual Report
  Sr. Community Services Supervisor Sevag Garabetian gave a report and PowerPoint presentation
  covering the following topics as they relate to Sparr Heights Community Center: history, center-
  based programs, Senior Nutrition Program, drop-in exercise classes, GCC Lifelong Learning
  Classes, children’s programs, Sparr-tacular day camps, Parent’s Night Out, and fiscal impact.

  Commissioners had no questions.

  E.  Section Activity Reports
  1.  Workforce Development
  Workforce Development Administrator Judith Velasco reported on the Verdugo CNC Machinist
  Academy graduation and open house, $400,000 from the Department of Rehabilitation (DOR)
  to provide work-based learning opportunities for youth with disabilities, and the Summer
  Training & Employment Program for Students (STEPS).

  Commissioners had no questions.

  2.  Recreation & Community Services
  Mr. Garabetian gave a report and PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics:
  Cesar Chavez Commemorative Event, Spring Eggstravaganza, programs at community
  centers, holiday celebrations for seniors, Therapeutic Recreation events, Youth & Family
  Services events, STAR Program, One Glendale After School Youth Sports Program
  Basketball Championship, Trails and Open Space events, and Go! Program.

  Commissioners had no questions.

  3.  Park Services
  Mr. Panossian provided a brief overview of work orders completed by Park Services staff in
  the months of March and April.

  Commissioners had no questions.
9.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 3:39 p.m.
